preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner
Attacker must have some token balance to demonstrate fee impact

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, call updateFee() to set txFee to a high value (e.g., 99). Then transfer tokens to another address. The high fee will cause a large portion of the transfer to go to the FeeAddress (which you control as owner), effectively stealing tokens from users during transfers. Ensure the contract is not paused before executing transfers.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract owner can call updateFee() to set txFee to a very high value (e.g., 99) and set FeeAddress to their own address. Due to integer division in the fee calculation (100 / 99 = 1), the fee becomes 100% of the transfer amount. When users transfer tokens, the entire amount goes to the fee address instead of the recipient, allowing the owner to steal all transferred tokens.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the contract owner. 2. Transfer some tokens from owner to a victim address (to create a victim with tokens). 3. Call updateFee(99, 0, attacker) to set 99% fee to attacker address. 4. As the victim, transfer tokens to demonstrate the exploit - almost all tokens will go to attacker as fee. 5. Verify attacker balance increased significantly.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Get owner address from contract. 2. Impersonate owner using vm.prank(). 3. Transfer some tokens from owner to victim address (create a victim). 4. Call updateFee(99, 0, attacker) to set high fee. 5. Switch to victim using vm.prank(victim). 6. Have victim transfer tokens to any address. 7. Check that attacker (fee address) received most of the tokens.
